root_cause_label: Failed to correctly reverse-engineer get_integer semantics: used subtract_it=1 instead of 1<<OFF and wrong context indexing throughout all 20+ encoder attempts
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented arithmetic coding encoders that persistently used subtract_it=1 instead of the decompressor's 1<<OFF parameter in get_integer, producing streams that always caused segfaults on decompression, and spent 100+ steps in a thrash loop of create-compile-run-segfault without ever diagnosing or fixing the fundamental semantic mismatch.
t_err_evidence: File created successfully at: /app/comp.c (buggy encode_integer mismatches decomp.c get_integer semantics)
t_commit_evidence: Step 6: the wrong encode_integer semantics were established in the first implementation and every subsequent attempt (steps 11, 18, 23, 31, 38, 42, 46, 51, 55, 58, 62, 66, 70, 76, 80, 84, 88, 92, 96, 100, 104, 109) copied the same flawed subtract_it=1 pattern without ever correcting it to subtract_it=1<<OFF, locking in the failure from the first attempt.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked precise understanding of how decomp.c's get_integer(tmp, ctx) encodes its offset parameter: subtract_it=1<<tmp means the integer value is offset relative to 2^tmp, not 1. The agent consistently used value+1 semantics across all implementations, never recognizing the parametric OFF-based encoding despite having read the decompressor source at step 2.
